newsitem.title: BELGIUM: WAIGEL GOLD PROPOSAL NO BOOK-COOKING - SOURCE.
newsitem.headline: WAIGEL GOLD PROPOSAL NO BOOK-COOKING - SOURCE.

text.p: German Finance Minister Theo Waigel's proposal to revalue Bundesbank gold reservers is in line with practice of most other European central banks and by no means a way of "cooking the books," an EU monetary official told Reuters.

"What the Bundesbank would do (if the proposal is followed) is precisely what other central banks are doing. It is not cooking its books, quite the opposite in fact," the official, who declined to be identified said.
"The Germans were among the last ones to stick to the principle of ultra-prudence," he said.

"The valuation of a gold reserve at market levels is the first step towards the expression of a potential capital gain, but this does not necessarily lead to a sale. All it does is reflect a true and fair view of the central bank balance sheet," the official, who is a specialist in central bank accounting standards, said.
He said it was standard practice for European central banks to revalue their gold hoards. Some do it yearly, some at longer intervals.
The Belgian central bank, for instance, revalues its gold once a year, in line with European Monetary Institute gold valuation methods for gold/ECU swaps.

The Belgian central bank applies the following method for determining the value: the price is either the average of the gold price at the London daily fixings in the second half of the year or the average of the two fixings in the second to last working day of the year, if the latter price is lower than the former. This way the bank takes the most conservative price.
The official said that Italy, the Netherlands, Denmark, France and Austria all had similar gold valuation procedures.
Many European central bank gold valuation procedures are based on an average price, to which often a discount is applied, as is the case in Austria and the Netherlands, the official said.
"The continental approach is to be very cautious in gold valuation," the official said.
-- Geert De Clercq, Brussels Newsroom +32 2 287 6813, Fax +32 2 230 7710
